release_slices.name: DGFY invite session context hotfix
release_slices.plain_english_purpose: Restore IMS and POS DGFY cashier/user invitation search when the browser still has an access token but lost the tenant/company context required by backend authorization.
release_slices.purpose: Restore IMS and POS DGFY cashier/user invitation search when the browser still has an access token but lost the tenant/company context required by backend authorization.
release_slices.implementation_summary: Repair tenant context before tenant-scoped API calls when an IMS/POS access token already exists but the company token is absent. The backend authorization remains fail-closed; the frontend refreshes the HttpOnly browser session to recover the tenant context before sending DGFY account-search and tenant-bridge requests. Platform-admin requests are explicitly excluded from forced tenant-context repair.
included_features: IMS DGFY account search tenant-context repair
POS cashier invitation tenant-context repair through the shared API interceptor
Regression tests for token-without-company-context DGFY search and tenant bridge requests
Regression test proving platform-admin requests are not forced into tenant context
excluded_features: Backend DGFY authorization, membership lookup, tenant-handler, database, migration, payment, checkout, and fiscal changes
Unrelated POS logical-terminal local worktree changes
Full seeded rendered QA and production UAT mutation; these are deferred under the owner-approved emergency QA lane

release_slices.regression_warning_summary: The shared frontend API interceptor now refreshes tenant context when an access token exists but the company token is missing. A regression could add extra refreshes or affect tenant-scoped IMS/POS requests; platform-admin routes are excluded.
potentially_affected_existing_behaviors: IMS Manage Users DGFY account search
Generic tenant-scoped API requests after browser reload or session-context loss
Platform-admin requests that intentionally do not use tenant context

documentation_closure.rationale: ADR 0028 already requires IMS and POS DGFY invitations to target registered DGFY accounts through tenant-authenticated flows. This release manifest documents the emergency repair, risk, validation, rollback, and accuracy requirements without changing backend authorization or architecture.

release_slices.adr_or_compliance: No new ADR or compliance declaration is required because this is a frontend session repair within the existing ADR 0028 DGFY invitation/auth boundary and changes no backend authorization, fiscal, payment, database, or API contract.
